page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable compute instance running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is powered by a 4th Generation Intel Xeon 8488C processor built on x86_64 architecture, providing 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The CPU features 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for matrix math acceleration.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not included, requiring external network-attached storage via EBS. In terms of connectivity, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs integrated into the configuration.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate top-tier execution across high-throughput memory and compute workloads. In memory bandwidth benchmarks, the system achieved a cached read score of 4711.73 GB/sec and an uncached read score of 212.09 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. Similarly, PassMark database operations (27825.62), static web serving throughput (68.72 GB/sec), and Redis SET throughput (70.49 million operations/sec) demonstrated top-quartile performance. General compute indicators also ranked high, with Geekbench single-core at 2104.0 and multi-core at 18702.0.

Tradeoffs center around its burstable CPU allocation model and the absence of discrete GPUs. While small-model LLM prompt processing reaches 2125.48 tokens/sec, medium-model (7B) prompt processing drops to 27.64 tokens/sec, landing in the bottom quartile. Synthetic stress-ng testing also exhibits middle-tier CPU ratings. Because the flex variant balances resource capacity with burstable utilization, it provides an economical option for varying workloads. It is best suited for application servers, static web delivery, Clang build pipelines, caching tiers, and relational or in-memory databases.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.16xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor at 3.2 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro System, the instance incorporates 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no onboard GPUs and offers no local instance storage. Benchmark tests reflect strong performance in Redis operations (70.49 million ops/sec), database operations, memory bandwidth, and static web serving, alongside competitive Geekbench compilation and multi-core metrics. Conversely, LLM inference on medium models shows hardware limitations inherent to CPU execution. With burstable allocation offering cost efficiency for fluctuating compute demands, m7i-flex.16xlarge is well fitted for web serving, database environments, CI/CD compilation, and enterprise caching layers.
